prompt: Create an ORIGINAL SNES-era fighting-game OFFICE CHAMPION celebration background. This is new game art for an original workplace arcade fighting game, with no commercial game sprites, no existing game logos, and no lettering. Canvas target 1024x896, aspect 8:7, a precisely composed 4x master for a 256x224 native SNES screen. Crisp bold dark-navy outlines, broad flat cel-cartoon shapes, royal navy, warm gold, ivory and restrained cool-blue shading, at most about 70 solid colors. Strong graphic silhouette, clean edges, no photographic texture, no dithering, no noisy scattered fine details. Composition coordinates below are expressed at the FINAL 256x224 native resolution; multiply coordinates by 4 for this master. The TOP BAND y0..39 must remain calm nearly solid royal navy (#111a3d) for a future heading drawn by the game. The RIGHT SIDE x156..255,y40..159 must remain calm nearly solid royal navy, completely EMPTY for a separate winner portrait the game will insert; DO NOT draw any portrait, face, placeholder, lettering, frame or box there. The BOTTOM BAND y160..223 must remain almost solid royal navy and empty for the game's quote and menu controls. All main illustration is concentrated on the LEFT x16..148,y48..152: a large, beautiful warm-gold championship cup with two broad handles, a bold star medallion with NO letters, on a short dignified navy-and-gold plinth that has a tiny recognizable computer-keyboard-like silhouette at its base. Main cup silhouette spans approximately x36..128,y54..145. Thick dark-navy contour, three broad golden planes, two ivory highlights and a cool shadow, unmistakable at native size. Behind the cup, only in the LEFT area, suggest an elegant Santiago office after hours with very subdued blue window panes and a simple Andes/night skyline, a discreet desk-lamp silhouette, and a few widely spaced gold diamond confetti pieces. These background shapes must stay quieter and darker than the cup, do not intrude into reserved right/top/bottom UI space. The art feels like an earned ending screen in a polished early-1990s arcade cartoon game: celebratory, warm, confident, spacious, with the trophy as the clear focal point. NO text anywhere, no watermark, no UI typography, no humans, no extra cups, no border around the full canvas. Opaque background, no transparency.
